postings.title: Principal Engineer, Autonomy
postings.description:
WHO WE ARE

We are hiring a Principal Engineer for Autonomy — the senior-most individual contributor in our autonomy organization. You will have the deepest hands-on technical ownership of one or more of Perception, Prediction, and Planning, with cross-stack influence across the rest of the autonomy stack. You will report directly to the VP of Engineering, with no direct reports of your own, but with the expectation that you set technical direction the rest of the autonomy team follows.

We are looking for someone who is excellent both at the systems level and at execution — a senior IC with the technical depth to anchor the hardest decisions in autonomy and the bias for shipping to convert those decisions into running code on a vehicle.




YOU WILL

You are the senior-most IC in autonomy, with the deepest technical ownership of either Perception, Prediction, or Planning (or any combination thereof) and influence across the rest of the stack.

 - Perception. Own the design and evolution of the perception stack — detection, classification, tracking, and multi-modal sensor fusion across the available modalities. Drive perception robustness across the long tail of real-world operating conditions, and set the direction for where and how deep learning is best applied across the perception pipeline.

 - Prediction. Own the prediction stack and the design of models for intent inference, behavior forecasting, and handling occlusions and edge cases. Set the direction for how prediction integrates with perception upstream and planning downstream.

 - Planning. Own the design of the planning and decision-making stack, from structured driving behaviors to the domain-specific maneuvers required for autonomous GSE operations. Set the direction for where learned components earn their place in the planner.

 - Cross-stack influence. Set the technical direction at the interfaces between your primary areas and the rest of the stack, and partner with the other senior engineers in autonomy to keep the system coherent end-to-end.

 - Autonomy architecture. Own the functional and SW architecture of the autonomy stack, and partner with neighboring teams towards its implementation.





YOU HAVE

 - 15+ years of hands-on experience building production autonomy systems, with strong technical depth across multiple modules (localization, perception, prediction, planning, controls). You think at the level of the autonomy system, not a single module.

 - Demonstrated track record of shipping autonomy components that have run in production on real vehicles at non-trivial scale — not just research prototypes or simulation results.

 - Prior experience as the most senior individual contributor in an autonomy organization — setting direction, mentoring staff/senior engineers, and partnering with engineering leadership without managing a team yourself.

 - Deepest technical depth in perception, prediction, or planning (ideally more than one of the three).

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals in C++ and Python. You write or review code that other senior engineers want to extend and trust in a safety-relevant system.

 - Fluency with modern deep learning for autonomy, including the practical realities of training, evaluation, deployment, and lifecycle management of models that have to work in the real world.

 - Experience working in or with ROS / ROS 2 and the distributed-systems realities of on-vehicle compute (real-time constraints, IPC, fault containment).

 - A bias for execution. You ship. You close out problems. You convert ambiguity into a plan and the plan into running code on a vehicle.




WE PREFER

 - Experience with safety-critical or functional-safety-relevant systems (ISO 26262, ISO 13849, SOTIF, or aerospace equivalents).

 - Experience operating in an Operational Design Domain that involves heavy interaction with humans, mixed traffic, or unstructured environments.

 - Familiarity with simulation-driven verification and the use of simulation as part of a CI/CD pipeline for autonomy.




WHY THIS ROLE AT AEROVECT?

 - A real ODD with real constraints. Airports are one of the few environments where commercial autonomy is genuinely viable today and where the path to removing the safety driver is concrete rather than speculative.

 - Scope. This is the senior autonomy IC role at AeroVect. You are the senior-most technical voice across Perception, Prediction, and Planning, with cross-stack influence across the rest of the autonomy stack.

 - A defined path to scale, not a science project. A real commercial deployment with a concrete path to removing the safety driver and scaling the fleet. Your work has a destination.

• Build the evaluation that turns a run into a pass/fail result, and the triage tools that autonomy engineers use on their own.
• Keep the simulation deterministic, reproducible, and fast as the number of scenarios grows.






WHAT YOU'LL NEED


• 3+ years of experience in simulation work for autonomous vehicles, robotics, or aerospace
• Strong Python, with a track record of maintainable code in a shared codebase
• Experience with a simulator such as CARLA, Applied Intuition, Foretellix, NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac Sim, Gazebo, or an in-house platform
• Understanding of simulation and modeling methodology: vehicle and actor models, fidelity, and how simulated results support claims about real-world behavior
• Docker, Linux, and distributed-systems fundamentals, with experience running GPU-based simulation
• Experience running simulation at scale in the cloud and in CI
• Experience debugging and profiling distributed, GPU-bound systems, and finding bottlenecks and failure modes in simulation output and telemetry
• Git and code review experience
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience






NICE TO HAVE


• 6+ years building simulation for autonomous vehicles, robotics, or aerospace

• Vehicle dynamics or actor behavior modeling

Mid level (typically 3-6 years): you own defined parts of the simulation end to end, ship them tested and documented, and make routine design decisions on your own.

Employee relations and compliance

Talent, performance, and rewards

postings.title: Senior Backend Engineer
postings.description:
WHO WE ARE

AeroVect is transforming ground handling with autonomy, redefining how airlines and ground service providers around the globe run day-to-day operations. We are a Series A company backed by top-tier venture capital investors in aviation and autonomous driving. Our customers include some of the world’s largest airlines and ground handling providers. For more information, visit www.aerovect.com http://www.aerovect.com.

As a Senior Backend Engineer you will design, build, and scale the backend systems that enable remote operators to monitor, support, and interact with our autonomous ground support equipment (AGSE) operating in live airport environments.

As our autonomous fleet expands across airports, remote assistance becomes a critical component of safe and reliable operations. You'll build the services that connect autonomous vehicles with remote operators, enabling real-time communication, vehicle monitoring, assistance requests, and operational decision-making.

This is a hands-on engineering role at the intersection of distributed systems, real-time communication, and autonomous vehicle operations. You'll work closely with autonomy, platform, infrastructure, and operations teams to develop reliable, low-latency backend services that support an increasingly large fleet of autonomous vehicles.

You'll have significant ownership over system architecture, reliability, and scalability, building production systems where performance and availability directly impact real-world operations.


YOU WILL

 - Design, develop, and maintain backend services powering AeroVect's remote assistance platform for autonomous vehicle operations.

 - Build reliable, low-latency communication systems between autonomous vehicles, cloud infrastructure, and remote operators.

 - Develop APIs and cloud backend services that enable vehicle monitoring, remote assistance requests, operator interactions, and fleet coordination.

 - Design and implement real-time data streaming and cloud event-driven architectures to support vehicle state updates, telemetry, and operational events.

 - Build scalable systems to manage remote assistance sessions, including request routing, operator assignment, session state, and lifecycle management.

 - Ensure backend systems are resilient to network interruptions, latency, and intermittent connectivity in real-world airport environments.

 - Develop robust mechanisms for authentication, authorization, auditing, and secure communication between vehicles and remote operators.

 - Build monitoring, logging, and observability capabilities to identify issues and maintain high system reliability.

 - Collaborate with autonomy and platform engineers to integrate remote assistance capabilities with vehicle software and fleet management systems.

 - Optimize backend performance, scalability, and fault tolerance as the number of deployed vehicles and remote assistance sessions increases.

 - Take end-to-end ownership of backend services, from system design and implementation through deployment, testing, and production support.


YOU HAVE

 - 5+ years of experience in backend software engineering, with a strong track record of designing and operating production-grade distributed systems.

 - Strong programming experience in Python, Go, C++, or similar backend languages.

 - Experience designing and building scalable backend services, APIs, and microservices architectures.

 - Strong understanding of distributed systems, concurrency, asynchronous processing, and fault-tolerant architectures.

 - Experience with real-time communication technologies such as WebSockets, gRPC, or similar protocols.

 - Hands-on experience with message brokers and event-driven systems such as Kafka, RabbitMQ, Redis Streams, or equivalent technologies.

 - Experience building and deploying cloud-native applications, preferably on AWS.

 - Familiarity with containerization and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.

 - Strong understanding of networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, HTTP, connection management, and latency optimization.

 - Experience designing systems for high availability, observability, and production reliability.

 - Ability to independently own complex technical projects and make sound architectural decisions in an evolving environment.

 - Strong communication skills and experience collaborating across software, infrastructure, and product teams.


WE PREFER

 - Experience building backend systems for autonomous vehicles, robotics, teleoperations, or remote assistance platforms.

 - Experience working with vehicle telemetry, fleet management, or real-time operational monitoring systems.

 - Knowledge of video streaming technologies such as WebRTC, RTSP, or other low-latency media protocols.

 - Experience developing systems that operate across unreliable or bandwidth-constrained networks.

 - Familiarity with safety-critical systems, operational safeguards, and secure remote interactions with physical devices.

 - Experience with edge-to-cloud communication architectures.

 - Experience building dispatching, scheduling, or resource allocation systems.

 - Previous experience in a fast-paced startup environment, building products and infrastructure from the ground up.
